incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 5201112222 - Customer 'Polaris Health' experiencing p99 streaming stalls and tail latency spikes (>5s) across a single-tenant pool. Paging on-call.

oncall-maria: got the page, looking now. First glance p99 is ~5.4s for streaming responses, overall p95 ~1.2s. Which endpoints impacted? any error spikes?

raj-eng: seeing the spike on /v1/chat/stream for model=redwood-llama-20b-quant. Error rate low, but streaming stalls (stuck at "data: [DONE]" delayed). Concurrency for that tenant jumped to ~1200 concurrent sessions around 12:34 UTC.

dave-sre: confirmed. Token emit rate normal, but telemetry shows many early KV cache misses and repeated KV loads. Looks like long prefix (~8k tokens) fanout pattern.

oncall-maria: are these long prefixes coming from a single customer job or many users? any pattern in prompts?

raj-eng: single tenant, but many distinct sessions. Prompts contain multi-file concatenation and some unicode / emojis. Example prefix snippet (sanitized):

```
<USER_PROMPT_PREFIX>
--- Patient history (redacted) ---
<ATTACHMENT_PLACEHOLDER>
🙂🤝
<END_PREFIX>
```

we're seeing prefix lengths 3-9k tokens and many repeated identical prefixes across sessions -> likely not sharing KV cache due to session IDs being unique.

slo-alert-bot: SLO BREACH: streaming p99 > 5s for Polaris Health - severity: high - triggered @oncall-maria @dave-sre @raj-eng

sre-jun: tagging infra. Could be KV cache keying issue (session-scoped cache) rather than tenant-scoped. If every session uses unique cache keys we lose cross-session prefix reuse.

eng-runtime-lead: quick mitigation options: 1) enable tenant-wide prefix canonicalization (merge identical prefixes into same cache key) 2) apply per-tenant concurrency cap 3) route overflow traffic to a smaller, faster model with lower KV-pressure 4) temporarily enable prefix-eviction tuning to prioritize shared prefixes.

oncall-maria: can we do an emergency traffic route to fallback model? how fast?

raj-eng: we can flip routing policy for the tenant to redwood-llama-7b-q4 at the load balancer for that tenant; TTL is immediate. Downsides: lower quality but much lower tail latency. I can apply a canary to 30% now.

dave-sre: before routing, apply short-term throttle to protect cluster: run this on the tenant route:

```
rbctl routes update --tenant polaris --concurrency-cap 200 --burst 300
```

That will shed excess concurrency and keep other tenants safe.

oncall-maria: doing throttle now. Running rbctl command... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incidents-bot: Command executed by oncall-maria at 12:48 UTC: rbctl routes update --tenant polaris --concurrency-cap 200 --burst 300

sre-jun: cluster telemetry shows concurrency dropping from 1200 -> 380 in ~30s. p99 drops to 2.3s but still above SLO.

eng-runtime-lead: push fallback canary to 40% for immediate relief.

raj-eng: canary applied: routing policy updated for polaris -> 40% to redwood-llama-7b-q4. Observing tail improvements.

oncall-maria: monitoring logs. p99 now 1.8s for streaming; p95 ~0.9s. Still seeing occasional stalls correlated with sessions that include multibyte emoji sequences.

dave-sre: digging into KV cache keys - discovered session-id prefixing in key derivation. Key = tenant_id + session_id + prefix_hash. So identical prefixes across different session_ids don't hit.

eng-runtime-lead: that's the root cause for cross-session reuse. Longer term we should change to tenant-scoped canonicalization with session-scoped salts for ephemeral per-session state.

sre-jun: immediate mitigation we can do: enable prefix canonicalization flag for polaris only. That will rekey to tenant_id + canonical_prefix_hash. Risk: might leak shared context if prefixes contain PII - ensure we sanitize.

raj-eng: we have a sanitize pipeline. I can enable canonicalization + prefix-sanitize for the tenant now. Command:

```
rbctl tenant update polaris --prefix-canonicalization enable --prefix-sanitize enable
```

oncall-maria: enable it. Doing the update now. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Command executed by oncall-maria at 12:53 UTC: rbctl tenant update polaris --prefix-canonicalization enable --prefix-sanitize enable

slo-alert-bot: SLO UPDATE: p99 dropped to 1.1s within 90s after canonicalization + routing changes. Still watching for regressions.

raj-eng: logs show KV cache hit rate for tenant increased from 12% -> 78% after canonicalization. Great.

dave-sre: re-evaluating autoscale: there was a short spike in GPU allocation due to the initial burst. No OOMs. We'll keep concurrency cap in place until traffic normalizes.

oncall-maria: customer-facing comms? Polaris CS already pinged us. We should draft a short note: root cause & mitigations taken, ETA for permanent fix.

eng-runtime-lead: agree. Draft:

"We observed a high-concurrency pattern from Polaris Health that caused inefficient KV cache usage due to session-scoped cache keys. This led to streaming tail latency spikes for a subset of requests. Immediate mitigations: temporary per-tenant concurrency cap, tenant prefix canonicalization + sanitize, and routing 40% traffic to a faster model. Result: p99 reduced from ~5.4s to ~1.1s. We're implementing a permanent fix to canonicalize prefix keys and improve cache hygiene."

oncall-maria: sending to support now. Also leaving follow-up tasks in JIRA: PERM-1234 (make tenant-canonicalization opt-in with audit), PERM-1235 (optimize cache-key derivation), PERM-1236 (add per-tenant autoscale alerts)

sre-jun: note for postmortem: consider adding a synthetic test for large-prefix fanout patterns (single-tenant multi-session) to catch regressions.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT 5201112222 update: mitigated. Severity -> reduced. Handing off to eng-runtime for follow-up. :handshake:

oncall-maria: handing off to @raj-eng and @eng-runtime-lead for post-incident action items. I'll update the on-call log and close paging after 1hr stable.

raj-eng: acknowledged. I'll own the rollout of the permanent canonicalization change and coordinate QA.

eng-runtime-lead: will schedule deploy and endpoint tests. Thanks everyone.

oncall-maria: closing the page at 13:50 UTC after 1hr stable. :white_check_mark: Summary saved to incident channel.
